name: Fermat difference-of-squares factorization
definition: For odd integer n≥3, start a=ceil(√n); increment a until s=a²−n=b² for integer b≥0; return u=a−b and v=a+b, with uv=n.
variables: n odd positive integer; a candidate midpoint; b nonnegative integer square root
assumptions: Exact integer arithmetic; odd integer n≥3; a trivial factor pair is allowed
limitations: At most (n+1)/2−ceil(√n)+1 square tests; Θ(n) tests for odd primes, exponential in bit length. Close factors require fewer tests. Counts exclude exact integer square root and bit-arithmetic costs. Returns one factor pair, not a complete prime factorization; (1,n) is allowed.
failure_conditions: Noninteger, even or n<3 input; overflow or resource exhaustion before completion. Do not treat an interrupted search as a primality result.
computation: Use integer square roots: a=isqrt(n−1)+1; compute s=a²−n and b=isqrt(s); if b²=s return (a−b,a+b) after verifying positivity and product; otherwise increment a.

source.citation: Number Theory: In Context and Interactive, Gordon College, §12.5.3 Fact 12.5.8 and Algorithm 12.5.10, https://www.math.gordon.edu/ntic/ntic2017/section-intro-factor.html ; Jose Capco, Algorithmic Number Theory Lecture 06, JKU, Algorithm 1, https://www3.risc.jku.at/education/courses/ws2018/algo_num_theory/lecture_06.pdf ; trivial pair, square case and exact bound independently derived.

mechanism_note: Every positive odd factor pair u≤v determines integer a=(u+v)/2 and b=(v−u)/2. Conversely a²−b²=n yields a positive pair. The trivial pair ensures termination at a=(n+1)/2; squares terminate immediately with b=0. First success gives the closest factor pair, since (u+n/u)/2 decreases for 1≤u≤√n. Distinct from trial division: searches midpoints for square differences rather than testing divisors.

name: Möbius function from prime multiplicities
definition: For n≥1 with complete prime factorization, μ(n)=0 if any prime multiplicity exceeds one; otherwise μ(n)=(−1)^k for k distinct primes.
variables: n positive integer; k number of distinct prime factors; μ(n) Möbius function
assumptions: Exact positive integers; verified complete factorization; empty multiset for n=1
limitations: For m supplied prime factors with multiplicity, expected O(m) hash-set operations or O(m log m) sorting comparisons; excludes verifying primality, product and obtaining factorization, as well as bit costs. Incomplete factorization cannot justify a value. Scalar arithmetic diagnostic, not an independent factorization method.
failure_conditions: Nonpositive or noninteger n, nonprime factors, inconsistent product or incomplete factorization.
computation: Validate positive n, every factor prime and product equal to n (empty product 1); use a set to detect repetitions; return zero for any repetition, otherwise return (−1)^m for m supplied factors.

source.citation: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions §27.2 equation 27.2.12, https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.2.E12 ; §27.6 equation 27.6.2, https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.6.E2 ; factor-list verification and operation costs independently derived.

required_inputs: Positive integer and complete verified prime factorization.
mechanism_note: The nonzero divisors contributing to Σ_(d|n) μ(d) correspond to subsets of the distinct primes; their signed sum is (1−1)^k for k distinct prime factors, hence zero for n>1 and one for n=1. This also provides a factorization-independent recursive reference. The squarefree parity function is distinct from the totient residue count but classified as diagnostic.
